items.excerpt: A faulty router setting may have triggered a nationwide U.S. air traffic ground stop earlier this month after overwhelming the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) communications network, CNN reported Wednesday, citing a source familiar with the investigation. Investigators believe they have identified the technical problem behind the disruption after successfully reproducing the failure in a laboratory, according to the report. The investigation has focused on a newly installed router at a remote radio communications site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where maintenance work was underway Nov. 13.
